ui.compare.title: Your choices and Fux's, weighed
ui.compare.intro: Where your notes and Fux's differ, a criterion Fux himself states sometimes favours one of them; only those places are listed.
ui.compare.none: Your counterpoint is identical to Fux's.
ui.compare.fuxBetter.imperfect: Fux's imperfect consonance serves his rule of more imperfect than perfect consonances (p. 46).
ui.compare.playerBetter.imperfect: Your imperfect consonance serves that rule (p. 46) better than Fux's perfect one here.
ui.compare.fuxBetter.motion: Fux arrives here by contrary or oblique motion, which he recommends (p. 45); you arrive by similar motion.
ui.compare.playerBetter.motion: You arrive here by contrary or oblique motion (p. 45); Fux arrives by similar motion.
ui.compare.fuxBetter.singable: Fux's line moves by smaller intervals there, so it is easier to sing (p. 53: everything in counterpoint should be very easy to sing).
ui.compare.playerBetter.singable: Your line moves by smaller intervals there, so it is easier to sing (p. 53).
ui.compare.equal: By Fux's stated criteria the two choices are equally good here; the difference is one of taste or of the line as a whole.
ui.compare.mann.player: Mann would have scored yours higher:
ui.compare.mann.fux: Mann would have scored Fux's higher:
ui.compare.mann.largeLeap: no leap larger than a fifth (the octave and the rising minor sixth excepted)
ui.compare.mann.leapsSameWay: no two leaps in the same direction
ui.compare.mann.uncompensated: a leap answered by motion the other way
ui.compare.mann.repeatedTwice: no tone repeated more than once
ui.compare.mannNote: Lines marked "Mann" apply Alfred Mann's melodic advice from the footnotes of his translation (1965, pp. 27 and 29): his, not Fux's.
ui.compare.taste: Where you differ from Fux, no criterion he states favours either choice: the differences are matters of taste.
ui.trio.title: Three voices: the cantus, your line and Fux's
ui.trio.intro: Sung together, the two counterpoints and the cantus make a three-voice texture. Each line against the cantus has been judged above; this reads what the third voice adds. Bars are numbered from 1.
ui.trio.introHalf: Sung together, the two counterpoints and the cantus make a three-voice texture. Each line against the cantus has been judged above; this reads what the third voice adds. Positions: bar number, a = downbeat, b = upbeat.
ui.trio.noFaults: No clash and no forbidden succession between your line and Fux's.
ui.trio.dissonanceWithBass: {where}: your line and Fux's make a dissonance ({detail}) against the lowest voice.
ui.trio.dissonanceBetweenUppers: {where}: your line and Fux's clash ({detail}) above the cantus (between upper voices only the fourth passes).
ui.trio.parallelPerfect: {where}: parallel {detail} between your line and Fux's.
ui.trio.directPerfectOuter: {where}: the outer voices (your line and Fux's) move in similar motion into a {detail}.
ui.trio.unison: {where}: your line and Fux's meet in unison; the texture thins to two voices there.
ui.trio.completeTriad: Complete harmony (three different notes, all consonant) in {n} places: {where}.
ui.trio.contrary: Your line and Fux's move in contrary motion in {n} places: {where}.

ui.export.help: Save what plays now, with every setting, as an audio file (MP3 or WAV)
ui.export.intro: The game plays the piece and records exactly what you hear (voices, versions, drums, continuo, tempo, humanising), then saves it as a file. Recording runs in real time; keep this tab open.
ui.export.kindQuestion: Mix mode? In mix mode you set up several loops, each its own way, and they are exported one after another as one continuous piece.
ui.export.kind.single.help: record what is set up now, for one or more passes (you can still mix live while it records)
ui.export.kind.mix.help: a different setup for each loop: sounds and mix, versions, your line, drums, continuo, tempo, humanising, which lines play
ui.export.mixHow: A bar at the bottom of the page then takes you through the loops: set up loop 1 (play it to hear it), press › for loop 2, and so on; a new loop starts as a copy of the one before. When they are ready, press Export.
ui.export.mixIntro: The {n} loops play one after another, each with its own setup, and are saved as one file. Recording runs in real time; keep this tab open.
ui.export.mixSetUp: set up this loop as you want it heard, then ›
ui.export.mixEditing: this loop is set up; change it, or move on
ui.export.mixPlaying: the loops play as you set them up
ui.export.ending.seamless.help: Cut exactly where the next pass would begin, so the file loops seamlessly in a player
ui.export.ending.final.help: The last pass ends as the piece ends: the drums' final stroke and the reverb's tail
ui.export.live: You can mix while it records: faders, balance, mute and solo, sounds, versions, drums, continuo and tempo all go into the file as you change them. Stop and save at any time.
ui.export.mixLive: mix live: every change is recorded
ui.export.mp3: recommended: small (about 1.4 MB a minute), plays everywhere, sends on WhatsApp as audio. On claude.ai it comes inside a .zip.
ui.export.wav: lossless, for editing elsewhere; about ten times larger
ui.export.zipped: {format} saved, inside a .zip (this viewer saves only some file types): unzip it to get the audio.
ui.export.failed: The audio could not be recorded in this browser.

ui.hold.help: Hold the note before on, for the chosen value; over the bar line it is the tie (key T)

ui.drums.title: Drums
ui.drums.loopHelp: Length of one loop of the pattern: ×2 stretches it over twice as many bars (half time), ÷2 fits it twice into a bar (double time); ×1.5 and ÷1.5 give the three-against-two relations (a loop of 2/3 bar is a triplet feel against the cantus). Click the length to return to one bar.
ui.drums.boxHelp: Choosing a pattern switches the drums on and plays one bar of it; a drum-machine pattern brings its machine's sound, and Sound plays any pattern on any kit. With the loop on, the last bar is a roll that leads back to bar 1 instead of a final crash. The timpani are tuned to the final of the mode and its fifth.
ui.drums.kit.tr808.help: After the Roland TR-808 (1980), all analog: a long, booming bass drum, a hissing snare, the metallic hats and the two-tone cowbell. Synthesized here, not sampled.
ui.drums.kit.tr909.help: After the Roland TR-909 (1983): a punchy swept bass drum, a bright snare and clap. Its cymbals were 6-bit samples on the original; here they are imitated.
ui.drums.kit.cr78.help: After the Roland CR-78 CompuRhythm (1978): soft, small analog voices, the ticking metal beat, tambourine and guiro.
ui.drums.kit.rhythmAce.help: After the Ace Tone Rhythm Ace (1967) and the preset rhythm boxes of the organ era: short, dull, plain sounds.
ui.drums.kit.sdsv.help: After the Simmons SDS-V (1981): toms and snare with a deep downward pitch bend.
ui.drums.pattern.electro.help: An early-80s electro groove on the 808: syncopated bass drum, clap, cowbell, conga.
ui.drums.pattern.slowjam.help: A soul ballad groove on the 808, with rim clicks and a low conga.
ui.drums.pattern.house.help: Four on the floor on the 909: clap on two and four, open hats on the off-beats.
ui.drums.pattern.techno.help: A driving 909 pulse with ride cymbal and off-beat hats.
ui.drums.pattern.newwave.help: A late-70s CR-78 pattern: soft kick and snare, ticking hats, tambourine and guiro.
ui.drums.pattern.rhythmbox.help: A preset-style beat from an organ-era rhythm box: kick, snare, claves and cymbal.
ui.drums.pattern.synthtoms.help: An 80s pattern on Simmons drums, with falling-pitch tom fills.
ui.drums.pattern.rock.help: Kick, backbeat snare and eighth-note hi-hat.
ui.drums.pattern.funk.help: Syncopated kick, ghost notes on the snare, sixteenth hats.
ui.drums.pattern.halftime.help: A heavy groove with the snare on the third beat, and a ride cymbal.
ui.drums.pattern.bossa.help: Rim clicks, soft kick and shaker.
ui.drums.pattern.conga.help: Congas over a cowbell bell pattern and a shaker.
ui.drums.pattern.clave.help: Son clave on claves, woodblock and bongos.
ui.drums.pattern.tribal.help: Djembe bass and slaps, frame drum and shaker.
ui.drums.pattern.taiko.help: Big drums, rim clicks and claps.
ui.drums.pattern.ritual.help: A slow heartbeat on the frame drum, with a triangle.
ui.drums.pattern.timpani.help: Timpani on the final and the fifth; a roll before the last bar, cymbals at the end.
ui.drums.pattern.march.help: Field drum, bass drum, cymbals and a timpano.
ui.drums.pattern.processional.help: Bass drum, soft timpani and a triangle.

ui.demo.help: Ready-made exercises with Fux's solutions, for trying the features
ui.demo.title: Demo
ui.demo.intro: Each Load puts Fux's own solution into the exercise, already judged, with his line shown: his playback, the comparison and the three-voice reading are open. Nothing here earns a star. Under each, what to try.
ui.demo.humaniseHelp: Plays with a performer's shaping: accented downbeats, a phrase arch, higher notes a little louder, detached repeated notes, a breath before leaps, a final ritardando, a few milliseconds of irregularity
ui.demo.humaniseTry: Switch it on and off while listening to the same exercise: the notes are the same, the performance is not. It applies to every playback, the saved pieces included.
ui.demo.allTitle: Every exercise with Fux's solution (his line with the cantus, on the current sound)
ui.demo.first.title: First species, cantus below (D)
ui.demo.first.try.1: Press ▶ to hear the line with the cantus; ⟲ switches the loop. Then Fux (his line alone) and Trio (yours and his together).
ui.demo.first.try.2: On the Contrapunctus strip, switch on I, R or C: each version gets a staff and a strip. Press Evaluate twice (off, on) to see each version judged below.
ui.demo.first.try.3: Save it with the floppy disk at the top, then open ♫ and play it from the list.
ui.demo.crossing.title: First species, cantus above (F)
ui.demo.crossing.try.1: Open Rules: the first hint explains when to write B♭ in this mode.
ui.demo.crossing.try.2: Drag one of your notes to another pitch (Fux's diamonds stay), press Evaluate, then read the comparison and the three-voice reading.
ui.demo.crossing.try.3: In the mixer, move Fux an octave with ‹ ›, and try solo (S) and mute (M) on each strip.
ui.demo.second.title: Second species, cantus below (D)
ui.demo.second.try.1: Two half notes against each whole note; the opening half rest is Fux's.
ui.demo.second.try.2: Turn the tempo knob up (to 240) while it plays; switch Drums on in the mixer and pick a pattern below.
ui.demo.second.try.3: Choose another instrument for the Contrapunctus: the family ‹ › and preset ‹ › arrows in the synth below the mixer.
ui.demo.softB.title: Second species, cantus above (F)
ui.demo.softB.try.1: Fux's line has B♭s where it would otherwise meet F in a tritone; compare with the hint under Rules.
ui.demo.softB.try.2: Press Trio and read the three-voice reading: where your line and Fux's would clash if sung together.
ui.demo.softB.try.3: Switch O off on the Contrapunctus strip with I on: the inversion takes the place of your line.
ui.demo.third.title: Third species, cantus below (D)
ui.demo.third.try.1: Four quarters against each whole note; the score is scaled down so that the whole exercise fits.
ui.demo.third.try.2: Switch Intervals on: the dissonant quarters are the passing notes, and in bar 3 a cambiata (a step down to a dissonant seventh, then a third down).
ui.demo.third.try.3: Select a quarter, type letters (each one moves on to the next quarter) and press Evaluate to see the dissonances judged.
ui.demo.fourth.title: Fourth species, cantus below (D), with continuo
ui.demo.fourth.try.1: Ligatures: each upbeat is held over the bar line, and the held note is dissonant (7) and resolves down to the sixth.
ui.demo.fourth.try.2: The continuo plays the suspensions as a continuo player would, figured 7 6, and waits for the resolution.
ui.demo.fourth.try.3: To write a tie, type the upbeat's letter and then T (or press Tie): the same note continues into the next bar.
ui.demo.fifth.title: Fifth species, cantus below (D): Aloysius's own example
ui.demo.fifth.try.1: Florid counterpoint: minims, crotchets, quavers in pairs, ligatures over the bar line. Switch Intervals on to see the suspensions (7 over the bar line, resolving to 6).
ui.demo.fifth.try.2: Clear all and write your own: choose a note value (keys 8, 4, 3, 2, 6, 1, or the note buttons), type the letters; T holds a note over the bar line.
ui.demo.fifth.try.3: Switch the inversion and the canon on (their numbered buttons on the mixer) and move them an octave away with ‹ ›: they move on the score too.
ui.demo.continuo.title: Basso continuo (second species, E)
ui.demo.continuo.try.1: The continuo is switched on (harpsichord): under the score, its keyboard part in small notes, with the figures under the bass.
ui.demo.continuo.try.2: Press ▶: the continuo plays with the two voices. Press Fux (realized for his line) and Trio (it only doubles the three voices).
ui.demo.continuo.try.3: On the Continuo strip, the B.c. button cycles what the score shows; click the strip's name for instruments (stile antico, cembalo, Hofkapelle), finals and passing fills.
ui.demo.continuo.try.4: Change the tempo while it plays: the continuo follows. Its fader, balance, mute and solo work like any strip's.
ui.demo.continuo.try.5: Delete some notes (select, then Delete) or write wrong ones: the continuo still plays and shows what it can, doubling (c.p.) where no chord fits.

ui.versions.help.original: Your line as written (the only one you can edit)
ui.versions.help.inversion: Inversion, as Bach mirrors: the final and the fifth trade places, the third stays
ui.versions.help.retrograde: Retrograde: your notes from last to first
ui.versions.help.canon: Canon at the unison: your line displaced by some slots, wrapping round to the first bars
ui.versions.hidden: Your written line is hidden; switch O back on to edit it.
ui.mixer.octaveHelp: Transpose this line by octaves when it plays (the score does not change)
ui.mixer.link: Link these two voices: they will share one sound
ui.mixer.unlink: Unlink: each voice keeps its own sound
ui.mixer.linkQuestion: Prior configurations will be lost: the {other} will take the Contrapunctus sound. Continue?
ui.compare.fuxBetter.variety: You repeat the previous note here; Fux moves on. Repetition is the cheapest way out of a bad progression, and Aloysius praises avoiding it for variety's sake (1725 p. 74).
ui.compare.playerBetter.variety: Fux repeats his previous note here and you move on, which gives your line more variety.

ui.view.namesHelp: Print the name of each note beside it
ui.view.intervalsHelp: Show the interval of each of your notes against the cantus, without judging them (Evaluate judges)
ui.loop.on: Loop is on: playback repeats until you stop it
ui.loop.off: Loop is off: playback stops at the end
ui.continuo.help: Basso continuo: a keyboard accompaniment, with its figured bass
ui.continuo.title: Basso continuo
ui.continuo.display.none.help: Show nothing of the continuo in the score
ui.continuo.display.figured.help: A small bass staff under the score, with the figures
ui.continuo.display.realization.help: The keyboard part (right hand and bass) in small notes, without figures
ui.continuo.display.both.help: The keyboard part with the figures under its bass
ui.continuo.preset.stileAntico.help: A soft chamber organ (stopped flute 8′ and a quiet 4′), as in church music in the old style
ui.continuo.preset.hofkapelle.help: The Vienna court chapel: organ and harpsichord, strings doubling the voices, cello and violone on the bass
ui.continuo.preset.theorbo.help: Theorbo (plucked, chords rolled, the bass in its long strings) with a bass viol sustaining the bass
ui.continuo.preset.pizzicato.help: A string band playing pizzicato: the chords plucked and plucked again on the upbeat, cellos and basses an octave apart
ui.continuo.preset.sostenuto.help: Sustained strings: the chords held with slow bows, cellos and basses on the bass line
ui.continuo.preset.brass.help: Sackbuts and cornetts: brassy, swelling chords, the bass on a low sackbut
ui.continuo.preset.analogPads.help: A vintage analog synthesizer: a slow, drifting string-machine pad for the chords, a resonant mono synth bass an octave down
ui.continuo.preset.electricPiano.help: An electric piano (bell-like, FM) for the chords, an upright bass plucked on the bass line
ui.continuo.preset.rockBand.help: A rock setup: electric bass with drive on the left hand; the right hand split between two guitars, an overdriven, singing lead on the top note and a clean, chorused rhythm guitar strumming the notes below
ui.continuo.finals.organist.help: The final chord complete, with a major (Picardy) third, as organists played it
ui.continuo.finals.strict.help: The final chord as octave and fifth, as Fux prescribes in three voices
ui.continuo.passing.help: Second species: stepwise passing notes in the right hand into leaps of a third or a fourth
ui.continuo.inegal.help: A stylistic liberty: the harpsichord's upbeat re-strike comes a little late
ui.continuo.boxHelp: The accompaniment is generated, for pleasure only, and plays no part in grading. In this demo it follows whatever is written now, solved or not.

tutor.result.cleared: [Placeholder] Aloysius approves: no rule is broken.
tutor.result.notCleared: [Placeholder] Aloysius points out what must be corrected.
tutor.rule.fs.vertical-consonance: [Placeholder] Only consonances are allowed in this species; this interval is a dissonance.
tutor.rule.fs.opening-perfect: [Placeholder] Begin with a perfect consonance (with the counterpoint below: the octave or unison, to stay in the mode).
tutor.rule.fs.final-octave-or-unison: [Placeholder] End on the octave or the unison.
tutor.rule.fs.cadence: [Placeholder] Before the final, the cantus below asks for a major sixth (the cantus above, a minor third), opening to the octave.
tutor.rule.fs.perfect-approach: [Placeholder] A perfect consonance may be reached only by contrary or oblique motion.
tutor.rule.fs.unison-only-at-ends: [Placeholder] The unison belongs only at the beginning and the end.
tutor.rule.fs.melodic-tritone: [Placeholder] Mi against fa: the leap of a tritone is forbidden.
tutor.rule.fs.melodic-major-sixth: [Placeholder] The leap of a major sixth is forbidden.
tutor.rule.fs.converging-leap-into-octave: [Placeholder] Do not leap into the octave or unison from a distant consonance with the voices converging.
tutor.rule.fs.unison-leap: [Placeholder] Do not leap out of, or into, the unison.
tutor.rule.fs.prefer-contrary-motion: [Placeholder] Use contrary or oblique motion as much as possible; here similar motion predominates.
tutor.rule.fs.prefer-imperfect-consonances: [Placeholder] Too many perfect consonances: Fux's rule asks for more thirds and sixths than unisons, fifths and octaves between the first and last bar.
tutor.rule.ss.downbeat-consonance: [Placeholder] The note on the downbeat must always be consonant.
tutor.rule.ss.passing-dissonance: [Placeholder] A dissonance on the upbeat is allowed only as a passing note, by step, filling a third.
tutor.rule.ss.cadence: [Placeholder] In the next-to-last bar: a fifth, then the sixth (cantus below) or the minor third (cantus above).
tutor.rule.ss.downbeat-succession: [Placeholder] The upbeat note is too short and too close to hide these fifths (or octaves) between the downbeats; a skip of a fourth or more would.
tutor.rule.ts.downbeat-consonance: The first of the four quarters, on the downbeat, must be consonant.
tutor.rule.ts.dissonance: A dissonant quarter must pass by step, continuing in the same direction; or, on the second quarter, it may be the cambiata: reached by a step down and left by a skip of a third down to a consonance.
tutor.rule.ts.cadence: In the next-to-last bar the last quarter must lead into the final: a major sixth above the cantus (cantus below), a minor third below it (cantus above).
tutor.rule.fos.arsis-consonant: The first note of a ligature, on the upbeat, must always be consonant.
tutor.rule.fos.resolution: A dissonance on the downbeat must be tied over from the upbeat and resolve by step down to a consonance.
tutor.rule.fos.ligature-kinds: This ligature is not allowed: from the unison to the second, or from the octave to the ninth, it hides two unisons or octaves (cantus below); the seventh resolving to the octave is avoided (cantus above).
tutor.rule.fos.cadence: In the next-to-last bar: the seventh tied over and resolving to the major sixth (cantus below), or the second resolving to the minor third (cantus above).
tutor.rule.fos.ligature-where-possible: Tie the upbeat over into the next bar wherever you can. Plain minims are fine where no ligature fits; leaving out one that fits is allowed only as often as Fux does it in this exercise.
tutor.rule.fis.downbeat-consonance: A note struck on the downbeat must be consonant; only a note tied over the bar line may be dissonant there.
tutor.rule.fis.suspension: This tied dissonance is not handled as Fux handles it: it must be prepared by a consonance and resolve a step down to a consonance, at once or on the half bar after consonant notes (and, cantus below, never unison to second or octave to ninth; cantus above, never seventh to octave).
tutor.rule.fis.weak-dissonance: A dissonance off the downbeat must pass by step in one direction, be the cambiata, or step to a neighbour and back (a quaver, or a crotchet on the second or fourth crotchet).
tutor.rule.fis.quavers: Quavers come two at a time, on the second or the fourth crotchet of the bar, never on the first or third.
tutor.rule.fis.ligature: A note is tied over the bar line only from the second half of the bar: the first note of a ligature is on the upbeat.
tutor.rule.fis.cadence: The next-to-last bar must end on the note below the final: the major sixth (cantus below) or the minor third (cantus above).
tutor.rule.fis.limping: Two crotchets at the start of the bar with no ligature after them make the melody limp, says Aloysius: tie them into a ligature, or go on with two more crotchets. Advice, not a precept.

hints.rules: Rules (breaking one means the exercise is not cleared)
hints.cadencePlain: Bar {bar}: no accidental is needed for the cadence in this mode.
hints.cadenceAltered: Bar {bar}: the cadence needs an accidental in this mode.
hints.rule.fs.vertical-consonance: Every vertical interval must be a consonance: unison, third, fifth, sixth or octave (or a compound of these). The fourth counts as a dissonance.
hints.rule.fs.prefer-contrary-motion: Use contrary or oblique motion as much as possible.
hints.rule.fs.perfect-approach: Reach a perfect consonance (unison, fifth, octave) only by contrary or oblique motion, never by parallel or similar motion.
hints.rule.fs.opening-perfect: Begin on a perfect consonance. With the counterpoint below the cantus, begin on the octave or unison, not the fifth, to stay in the mode.
hints.rule.fs.final-octave-or-unison: End on the octave or the unison.
hints.rule.fs.cadence: In the next-to-last bar: a major sixth when the cantus is below, a minor third when the cantus is above; then the octave or unison.
hints.rule.fs.unison-only-at-ends: Use the unison only in the first and the last bar.
hints.rule.fs.converging-leap-into-octave: Do not leap into an octave or unison from a more distant consonance with the voices converging.
hints.rule.fs.unison-leap: Do not leap out of a unison, or into one.
hints.glance.compounds: Compound intervals above the octave count as their simple form.
hints.glance.parallelBan: Parallel fifths and octaves: the most strictly forbidden progression.
hints.def.perfect: Perfect consonances: the unison, the fifth and the octave. They sound complete and stable, so the rules limit how they may be approached.
hints.def.imperfect: Imperfect consonances: thirds and sixths, major or minor. They sound sweet but not final, and may be approached by any motion.
hints.def.dissonance: Dissonances: seconds, fourths, the tritone and sevenths. In first species every vertical interval must be a consonance, so none of these may appear.
hints.def.unison: Unison (1): both voices sing the same pitch.
hints.def.fifth: Perfect fifth (5): seven semitones, e.g. C up to G.
hints.def.octave: Octave (8): the same note twelve semitones higher, e.g. C to the next C.
hints.def.m3: Minor third: three semitones, e.g. A up to C.
hints.def.M3: Major third: four semitones, e.g. C up to E.
hints.def.m6: Minor sixth: eight semitones, e.g. E up to C.
hints.def.M6: Major sixth: nine semitones, e.g. C up to A.
hints.def.second: Seconds: neighbouring notes (one or two semitones apart). Dissonant.
hints.def.fourth: Perfect fourth: five semitones. Between two voices it counts as a dissonance here.
hints.def.tritone: Tritone: six semitones (an augmented fourth or diminished fifth, e.g. F to B). Dissonant; Fux calls it 'mi contra fa'.
hints.def.seventh: Sevenths: ten or eleven semitones. Dissonant.
hints.def.compound: A compound interval is wider than an octave; it behaves like its simple form an octave smaller (a tenth like a third, a twelfth like a fifth).
hints.def.parallel: Parallel motion: both voices move in the same direction and keep the same interval (e.g. fifth to fifth). Into a perfect consonance it is forbidden.
hints.def.similar: Similar motion: both voices move in the same direction but by different amounts, so the interval changes. Into a perfect consonance it is forbidden.
hints.def.oblique: Oblique motion: one voice holds its note while the other moves.
hints.def.contrary: Contrary motion: the voices move in opposite directions. Fux recommends it as much as possible.
hints.rule.fs.prefer-imperfect-consonances: Use more imperfect consonances (thirds, sixths) than perfect ones (unisons, fifths, octaves) between the first and the last bar.
hints.glance.dissonant2: Dissonances (only on the upbeat, passing by step)
hints.def.dissonance2: Dissonances: seconds, fourths, the tritone and sevenths. In second species the downbeat note is always consonant; the upbeat note may be dissonant only when it passes by step from the note before to the note after, filling a third.
hints.glance.dissonant3: Dissonances (off the downbeat: passing by step, or the cambiata)
hints.def.dissonance3: Dissonances: seconds, fourths, the tritone and sevenths. In third species the first quarter is always consonant; another quarter may be dissonant when it passes by step in one direction, or as the cambiata: the second quarter, reached by a step down and left by a skip of a third down to a consonance.
hints.glance.dissonant4: Dissonances (on the downbeat, tied over and resolved down by step)
hints.def.dissonance4: Dissonances: seconds, fourths, the tritone and sevenths. In fourth species the dissonance comes on the downbeat, tied over from a consonant upbeat, and resolves by step down to a consonance on the next upbeat.
hints.glance.dissonant5: Dissonances (tied over the bar line and resolved down; or passing, cambiata, neighbour)
hints.def.dissonance5: Dissonances: seconds, fourths, the tritone and sevenths. In florid counterpoint each value keeps its species' treatment: on the downbeat only tied over and resolved a step down (the resolution may be decorated); elsewhere passing by step, the cambiata, or a quick neighbour and back.
hints.device.rest: A half rest may take the place of the first note.
hints.device.leap: When the voices are so close that contrary motion is impossible, a leap of a minor sixth (upward) or of an octave opens the space again.
hints.cadenceSixth: Bar {bar}: the fifth on the downbeat would be mi against fa here, so a sixth replaces it.
hints.lookAhead: Decide the ending before you begin, and look one or two bars ahead while writing.
hints.rule.ss.downbeat-consonance: The note on the downbeat must be a consonance.
hints.rule.ss.passing-dissonance: The upbeat note may be a dissonance only when it moves by step from the downbeat note to the next note, in the same direction (filling a third); after or before a leap it must be consonant.
hints.rule.ss.perfect-approach: Reach a perfect consonance only by contrary or oblique motion, as in first species.
hints.rule.ss.prefer-contrary-motion: Use contrary or oblique motion as much as possible.
hints.rule.ss.opening-perfect: Begin (after the rest, if any) on a perfect consonance; with the counterpoint below, on the octave or unison.
hints.rule.ss.final-octave-or-unison: End on the octave or the unison.
hints.rule.ss.melodic-major-sixth: Never leap a major sixth (the minor sixth upward is allowed).
hints.rule.ss.converging-leap-into-octave: Do not leap into an octave or unison from a more distant consonance with the voices converging.
hints.rule.ss.cadence: Next-to-last bar: a fifth on the downbeat, then a major sixth (cantus below) or a minor third (cantus above) on the upbeat.
hints.rule.ss.downbeat-succession: Read the downbeats as if the upbeat were absent when the upbeat is reached by a step or a skip of a third: no fifths or octaves in a row, and no similar motion into a perfect consonance. A skip of a fourth or more from the downbeat frees the progression.
hints.rule.ss.unison-only-at-ends: No unison on a downbeat except in the first and last bars (a unison on the upbeat is allowed, as in Fux's own examples).
hints.rule.ss.prefer-imperfect-consonances: Prefer imperfect consonances (thirds, sixths) on the downbeats.
hints.cadence2: Bar {bar}: {fifth} ({fifthNote}) on the downbeat, then {sixth} ({sixthNote}) on the upbeat.
hints.rule.ts.downbeat-consonance: The first quarter of each bar must be a consonance.
hints.rule.ts.dissonance: Off the downbeat, a dissonant quarter must be a passing note (by step, in one direction) or the cambiata (second quarter, a step down, then a skip of a third down to a consonance).
hints.rule.ts.cadence: Next-to-last bar: end on the note below the final, a major sixth (cantus below) or a minor third (cantus above).
hints.rule.ts.opening-perfect: Begin on a perfect consonance; with the counterpoint below, on the octave or unison.
hints.rule.ts.final-octave-or-unison: End on the octave or the unison.
hints.rule.ts.perfect-approach: Reach a perfect consonance only by contrary or oblique motion (across the bar line, where both voices move).
hints.rule.ts.melodic-major-sixth: Never leap a major sixth (the minor sixth upward is allowed).
hints.rule.ts.converging-leap-into-octave: Do not leap into an octave or unison from a more distant consonance with the voices converging.
hints.rule.ts.unison-only-at-ends: No unison on a downbeat except in the first and last bars.
hints.rule.fos.arsis-consonant: The upbeat that starts a ligature must be consonant (an untied upbeat may pass by step, as in second species).
hints.rule.fos.resolution: A dissonant downbeat must be tied from the upbeat and resolve by step down to a consonance.
hints.rule.fos.ligature-kinds: Cantus below: 2-1, 4-3, 7-6, 9-8, but never unison to second or octave to ninth. Cantus above: 2-3, 4-5, 9-10; not 7-8.
hints.rule.fos.cadence: Next-to-last bar: 7 tied, resolving to the major sixth (cantus below); 2 tied, resolving to the minor third (cantus above).
hints.rule.fos.ligature-where-possible: A ligature in every bar where possible; plain minims only where none fits. Leaving out one that fits: as often as Fux does in the exercise.
hints.rule.fis.downbeat-consonance: Every note struck on a downbeat is consonant.
hints.rule.fis.suspension: Tied over the bar line a dissonance is prepared and resolves a step down: at once, or on the half bar after consonant notes (Fux's 'variations', p. 76).
hints.rule.fis.weak-dissonance: Off the downbeat: a passing note, the cambiata, or a neighbour and back (quavers; a crotchet on the 2nd or 4th crotchet).
hints.rule.fis.quavers: Two quavers, on the 2nd or 4th crotchet; never on the 1st or 3rd.
hints.rule.fis.ligature: Ties over the bar line start on the upbeat half.
hints.rule.fis.cadence: Next-to-last bar: end on the major sixth (cantus below) or the minor third (cantus above), as Fux always does, from a tied 7 or 2.
hints.rule.fis.limping: Advice: two crotchets opening a bar want a ligature after them, or two more crotchets.
hints.rule.fis.opening-perfect: After the half rest, begin on a perfect consonance; with the counterpoint below, on the octave or unison.
hints.rule.fis.final-octave-or-unison: End on the octave or the unison.
hints.rule.fis.perfect-approach: Reach a perfect consonance only by contrary or oblique motion.
hints.rule.fis.melodic-major-sixth: Never leap a major sixth (the minor sixth upward is allowed).
hints.rule.fis.converging-leap-into-octave: Do not leap into an octave or unison from a more distant consonance with the voices converging.
hints.rule.fis.unison-only-at-ends: No unison on an untied downbeat except in the first and last bars.
hints.rule.fos.opening-perfect: After the half rest, begin on a perfect consonance; with the counterpoint below, on the octave or unison.
hints.rule.fos.final-octave-or-unison: End on the octave or the unison.
hints.rule.fos.perfect-approach: Reach a perfect consonance only by contrary or oblique motion.
hints.rule.fos.melodic-major-sixth: Never leap a major sixth (the minor sixth upward is allowed).
hints.rule.fos.converging-leap-into-octave: Do not leap into an octave or unison from a more distant consonance with the voices converging.
hints.rule.fos.unison-only-at-ends: No unison on an untied downbeat except in the first and last bars.

study.title: Lectio · {name}
study.intro: Fux's Latin is quoted from the Vienna print of 1725 with our translation; the dialogue is paraphrased; Alfred Mann's footnotes (The Study of Counterpoint, Norton, 1965) are quoted and marked as his, not Fux's.
study.fuxCite: Fux, Gradus ad Parnassum (1725), p. {page}; our translation
study.mannCite: Alfred Mann (translator's note), The Study of Counterpoint, p. {page}
study.mannCiteNote: Alfred Mann (translator's note), The Study of Counterpoint, p. {page}, n. {note}

help.howto: Write a counterpoint against Fux's cantus firmus: click your staff (or use the keys) to place notes, then Evaluate. Aloysius marks what breaks a rule; a clean result earns the star. Once cleared, compare with Fux's own solution and listen to both. Rules lists what applies here; Lectio is the study of Fux's text.
help.mouse: Mouse: click your staff to write; click a note and drag it to move it; click below or above the staves to select a bar.
help.keys.move: Previous / next note (stay a moment to hear it)
help.keys.step: Move the note up / down a step; right after a letter, the note just written. With Shift: an octave
help.keys.letter: Write that note, in the octave nearest the last one, and move on to the next
help.keys.rest: Rest (the first half of second and fourth species)
help.keys.tie: Repeat the previous note; in fourth species, the tie over the bar line; in fifth species, hold the note on (over the bar line, the tie)
help.keys.tracks: Switch track 1-9 of the mixer on or off (the number on its button), as in Ableton Live
help.keys.value: Fifth species: the value written next: quaver, crotchet, dotted crotchet, minim, dotted minim, whole bar
